flaps._comment: A32NX_FLAPS_HANDLE_INDEX is documented as the physical flap handle position: 0=0, 1=1/1+F, 2=2, 3=3, 4=FULL.

lvars._comment: A32NX LVARs are covered by authoritative profile sources. AP and A/THR use FlyByWire's current 0/1 FCU light readbacks; the older A32NX_AUTOPILOT_1_ACTIVE compatibility variable is explicitly deprecated in the published API. FCU windows use the published display-value interfaces.
lvars._commentFlaps: A32NX_FLAPS_HANDLE_INDEX is documented as the physical flaps handle position: 0=0, 1=1/1+F, 2=2, 3=3, 4=FULL. Flight Fabric uses profile flap LVARs before SimConnect flap mapping.

spoilers._comment: The cited FlyByWire interface supplies the intended armed state through A32NX_SPOILERS_ARMED and a 0-1 handle fraction through A32NX_SPOILERS_HANDLE_POSITION; the standard SimConnect armed field is not used for this profile.

lvars._commentParkingBrake: The cited FlyByWire interface supplies the intended parking-brake lever state through A32NX_PARK_BRAKE_LEVER_POS (0=released, 1=set); the standard SimConnect field is not used for this profile.

controls._comment: Aircraft-specific cockpit writes resolve only through the exact-profile trusted fbw-a32nx adapter. The adapter exposes fixed documented LVAR values and documented SimConnect events behind fresh readback, stable-simulator-state checks, cooldown and no-retry guards. Standard gear and flap actions remain available through the narrow shared fallback.

meta.notes: FlyByWire A32NX (Airbus A320neo). Activates the trusted A32NX aircraft page with 119 documentation-backed logical read fields and 230 fixed semantic actions spanning FCU mode buttons, EFIS/ND selectors, exterior lights, signs, electrical, APU, pneumatic, air conditioning, anti-ice, ADIRS, brakes, spoilers, engine controls, switching, weather radar, ATC/TCAS, RMP and ECAM. Every aircraft-specific action requires the exact bundled profile, a supported bounded transport, fresh preflight readback, per-control cooldown and post-write confirmation; routes never retry. Irreversible fire/IDG/oxygen actions, presets, pushback motion, delayed landing-light sequences and unsupported custom FCU set events remain excluded.

Fixed event routes covered here are STROBES_SET, BEACON_SET, WING_SET, NAV_LIGHTS_SET, LOGO_LIGHTS_SET, CABIN_SEATBELTS_ALERT_SWITCH_TOGGLE, ENGINE_BLEED_AIR_SOURCE_TOGGLE, ANTI_ICE_TOGGLE_ENG1, ANTI_ICE_TOGGLE_ENG2, TOGGLE_STRUCTURAL_DEICE, TOGGLE_FLIGHT_DIRECTOR, AP_LOC_HOLD, AP_APR_HOLD, AP_ATT_HOLD, AP_MACH_HOLD, AP_VS_HOLD, SPOILERS_ARM_TOGGLE, AUTOPILOT_OFF, AUTOPILOT_ON, AUTO_THROTTLE_DISCONNECT, AUTO_THROTTLE_ARM, FUELSYSTEM_VALVE_CLOSE, FUELSYSTEM_VALVE_OPEN, TURBINE_IGNITION_SWITCH_SET1, TURBINE_IGNITION_SWITCH_SET2 and SPOILERS_SET. The page identifies read/write status and value semantics for FCU/EFIS, exterior lights, signs, electrical, ADIRS, APU, air conditioning, anti-ice, autobrake, switching, ECAM, RMP, weather radar, ATC/TCAS, engine, spoiler and parking-brake controls. knownIssues: Most expanded routes are documentation-backed but have not been live-validated across every stable and development A32NX release. A selector-only or otherwise cosmetic write fails with a confirmation timeout when the configured logical field does not reach the requested value; a matching selector readback still does not prove every downstream aircraft-system effect.

FlyByWire states that its Flight Deck API table can lag current development. The adapter therefore uses only fixed bounded values, requires a fresh decodable preflight, serializes each physical control group, applies a 750 ms cooldown, never retries, and requires a newer confirming readback after dispatch.

Strobe coordinates LIGHTING_STROBE_0, STROBE_0_AUTO and STROBES_SET, then confirms actual LIGHT STROBE output for OFF/ON or the AUTO flag for AUTO. It still needs combined selector, AUTO and exterior-output validation on current aircraft builds.

Landing, nose and runway-turnoff lights remain monitoring-only because FlyByWire documents coordinated circuit, retraction and 8-10 second extension behavior that the bounded sequence transport cannot perform atomically.

Toggle-only standard events are presented as explicit targets only because the provider first requires a fresh matching readback and skips dispatch when the requested target is already satisfied. A changed target is dispatched once and must confirm.

FlyByWire custom FCU set/push/pull events are not exposed because the current native runtime does not advertise custom InputEvent execution. Only the documented standard SimConnect FCU mode events with direct light readback are enabled.
Fire, oxygen, irreversible IDG disconnect, flight-control-computer, preset loading/saving, pushback motion, raw flight axes and momentary controls without durable readback remain excluded.

Wipers remain excluded because the published interface requires indexed electrical-circuit power events and the current trusted integration transport does not provide an independently confirmed, position-safe indexed circuit route.
